findings.claim: The learning/control support is the score-clock window [0.0, 0.49] with 50 observed score nodes at 0.01 spacing; the objective is final predicted target affinity primary, with validity and strain secondary and coordinate control only.

For landmark_00_local_dx the observed endpoint-world coordinate contrast is non-monotone across the window: it rises to a positive peak near t~0.11, falls to a negative trough near t~0.19, partially recovers, and ends near zero (last_z ~0.18). The whole-window mean is near zero (whole_window_z ~ -0.18), so the net displacement over the window is small despite large internal excursions.

The landmark_00_local_dx trend is not well described by a low-degree polynomial (polynomial_accepted=false, relative_node_RMSE ~0.78) and shows 6 sign changes with 9 strong sign conflicts across 14 independent batches, so a single global monotone direction is not supported for this coordinate.

hypotheses.direction: test staged relevance (S1 observed-to-static) versus the constant-blend control (S2) at fixed dose; do not assume a monotone coordinate target
hypotheses.falsifier: If the staged schedule produces no reproducible difference in the landmark_00_local_dx contrast trajectory versus the constant-blend control across independent batches, the stage-dependent relevance hypothesis is not supported.
hypotheses.observable: landmark_00_local_dx endpoint-world coordinate contrast over the observed score nodes
hypotheses.scope: all seeds over the observed score-clock window [0.0, 0.49]; fixed dose_factors=1
hypotheses.statement: A stage-dependent teacher-relevance schedule (early same-clock historical forecasts blending toward frozen static teachers) is worth testing at fixed dose for the landmark_00_local_dx coordinate, because the observed contrast is strongly time-dependent (early positive excursion, mid-window negative excursion, late return toward zero) rather than stationary.

hypotheses.direction: retain the affinity objective; treat the sign change as a diagnostic only
hypotheses.falsifier: If the contrast sign change is not reproducible across independent batches, it is noise rather than a stage diagnostic.
hypotheses.observable: sign and magnitude of the landmark_00_local_dx contrast at early versus mid-window score nodes
hypotheses.scope: all seeds over the observed window
hypotheses.statement: The sign reversal in the landmark_00_local_dx contrast (positive early, negative mid-window) is a diagnostic of changing regional direction, not permission to reverse the affinity objective; the coordinate target should remain the final predicted target affinity.

limitations: Only one coordinate feature (landmark_00_local_dx) was read in detail; the remaining 199 curve features were not individually inspected, so no claim is made about their temporal behavior.
Stage profiles and temporal profiles are unavailable; no data-derived stage knot is supported, so any phase knot remains an experimental hypothesis rather than a discovered stage.

The observed contrast is a coordinate proxy in predicted endpoint world coordinates; it does not by itself specify an absolute coordinate target, spatial gradient, or any energy/chemical-interaction interpretation.
Selection preference and survival are not established here as final affinity improvement; no decoded final affinity labels were observed.
